epic_title: Architecture, boundaries, testability and release quality
summary: ARCH defines module boundaries, test seams, and release gates. User-visible behaviour belongs to the other epics.

stories.title: Layered architecture with a single allowed dependency direction
stories.story: As a maintainer extending Calendaric, I want the codebase organized into layers with one allowed dependency direction, so that I can change one concern without having to understand or risk breaking the others.
stories.rationale: The map shows the old code mixing note IO, date parsing, settings resolution and UI inside single files, and reaching into other plugins' internals from three separate layers at once.

acceptance_criteria.given: a module in the view layer (calendar rendering, settings tab, modals)
then: it imports only from the domain layer and from interfaces that layer defines for date, note, and settings logic
it contains no import of the vault-IO adapter layer
it contains no import of the cross-plugin-integration layer

acceptance_criteria.given: the domain layer (period and date logic, template-token resolution, settings validation)
then: it contains no import of the "obsidian" package
it contains no import of any adapter module or any view module

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin lifecycle module where dependencies are connected
then: it is the only module allowed to import from every layer
no other module imports the plugin lifecycle module

acceptance_criteria.given: a change introduces an import from the view layer into the vault-IO layer
then: the check fails
the check names the offending file and the disallowed import

acceptance_criteria.given: any layer other than the cross-plugin-integration layer needs information about a companion plugin (Periodic Notes, Templater, or any other)
then: it is obtained only through a typed function exported by the integration layer
no other layer imports a companion plugin's module directly

acceptance_criteria.given: the codebase makes any desktop-only API call (an Electron or Node capability not available on mobile)
acceptance_criteria.when: its imports and call sites are inspected
then: every desktop-only import and call is confined to one named adapter boundary
view modules and settings modules depend only on that adapter boundary's interface, never on the desktop-only API directly

stories.title: One implementation per shared concept
stories.story: As a maintainer, I want each date-parsing rule, filename-matching rule, and shared type defined exactly once in the codebase, so that fixing or extending a rule requires exactly one change instead of several coordinated ones.
stories.rationale: The map's most repeated finding is duplication: a date/time template-token pattern copy-pasted across five note-creation functions, two independently-diverging prefix-match implementations across the source repositories, a dev-plugin-id detection probe duplicated at six call sites across four functions in two repos, and (inside the target repository itself) a period-granularity type declared three times independently.

acceptance_criteria.given: day, week, month and year make up the first release's supported set of period granularities, and quarter is a reserved value that is not part of that release set
acceptance_criteria.when: that set is declared as a type
then: exactly one module owns the declaration
the declaration names quarter as reserved rather than as a supported release granularity
every other module that needs the type imports it from that one module
no module independently redeclares an equivalent type

acceptance_criteria.given: a filename needs to be parsed into a date, whether by strict matching or by prefix-tolerant matching
acceptance_criteria.when: two different granularities or two different call sites need that parsing
then: both call the same shared parsing function
no second, independently-maintained parsing routine exists in the codebase

acceptance_criteria.given: a date or time template token is resolved for a note
then: it executes through one shared token-resolution function
no granularity has its own copy of the resolution logic

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin needs to detect whether a companion plugin or feature is present
then: it exists in exactly one function that every caller uses
no second inline copy of the same detection logic exists elsewhere in the codebase

acceptance_criteria.given: a second implementation of a parser, a matcher, a shared type, or a detection routine is added anywhere in the codebase
acceptance_criteria.when: a duplication check runs over the source
then: the check flags the duplicate before the change can merge

decisions.title: The first release supports day, week, month and year; quarter is reserved
decisions.decision: The set of granularities the first release supports is day, week, month and year. Quarter is a reserved value: the type may name it and configuration may round-trip it, but no command is generated for it, no note is created for it, and no view offers it. Anything asking for quarter behaves the same way as any other granularity that is not enabled.
decisions.rationale: ARCH called quarter supported, NOTE used it as the example of an unsupported granularity, ICE-01 deferred it, and CMD still listed it for generated commands and startup opening. An agent reading the backlog could not tell whether quarter paths must work. This vault has quarter disabled, so nothing is lost by reserving it.

stories.title: Testable without a running Obsidian
stories.story: As someone maintaining Calendaric, I want the logic that decides what happens — not only pure date math — to be verifiable by an automated test, so that a change to note creation, settings resolution, or cross-plugin detection is checked by a test run instead of a manual reload-and-click pass.
stories.rationale: The target repository currently tests only pure functions; everything that touches the Obsidian API is untested, and its test double covers only three classes. Other epics list failure paths — a missing folder, an invalid format, a file that already exists, an absent template, an unparseable date — that this epic's testing seam must make reachable.

acceptance_criteria.given: a function that decides what note to create, open, or update
acceptance_criteria.when: it needs data from the vault or the app
then: it receives that data through an interface passed to it as a parameter or dependency
a test can supply a substitute for that interface without touching a real Obsidian instance
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/notes/noteCreate.test.ts, src/notes/noteOpen.test.ts — createNote/openNote/openNoteInNewTab now take VaultPort/WorkspacePort instead of the raw Obsidian App; all covered by FakeVaultPort/FakeWorkspacePort.

acceptance_criteria.given: the substitute used to stand in for the vault and workspace in tests
acceptance_criteria.when: a test exercises vault or workspace behaviour
then: the substitute covers every capability the plugin actually calls: file read, file write, file creation, workspace pane opening, and companion-plugin lookup
no capability the plugin calls is left uncovered by the substitute
acceptance_criteria.evidence: FakeVaultPort/FakeWorkspacePort cover file read/write/create and workspace pane opening (src/notes/noteCreate.test.ts, src/notes/noteOpen.test.ts). Companion-plugin lookup is already exercised without a running Obsidian by the pre-existing src/settings/dailyNotesImport.test.ts (its own hand-rolled App substitute, predating this ticket) — the capability is not left uncovered, though it is not yet unified under this ticket's VaultPort/WorkspacePort shape; that unification is US-ARCH-01/02 territory, not this ticket's.

acceptance_criteria.given: a named failure path (target folder missing, filename format invalid, note already exists at the target path, configured template absent, or date string unparseable)
then: a test exercises that failure path without a running Obsidian instance
the test asserts the observable outcome of that failure
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/notes/noteCreate.test.ts — 'creates the missing target folder', 'propagates the failure when a note already exists', 'creates an empty note when the configured template is absent', plus two seam-only proofs for 'invalid filename format' and 'unparseable date string' (FMT validation logic itself does not exist yet; these prove the port carries the rejection through).

acceptance_criteria.given: the domain layer's own test suite (period logic, template-token resolution, settings validation)
then: they execute with no dependency on the "obsidian" package, including its test double
acceptance_criteria.evidence: grep confirms src/notes/templateTokens.ts has no obsidian import; vitest: src/notes/templateTokens.test.ts (13 tests) runs with no obsidian module resolution.

acceptance_criteria.given: a change adds code that touches the vault, the workspace, or a companion plugin's API
acceptance_criteria.when: that change lands with no accompanying test exercising it through the substitute
then: the test-coverage gate for that layer fails
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Descoped by the orchestrator's own dispatch brief, section 5 (out of scope: building the automated CI coverage gate).
acceptance_criteria.not_applicable_because: Building an enforced, automated CI coverage gate for this criterion was explicitly out of scope for this ticket (orchestrator's own dispatch brief, section 5): a hand-written test alongside new vault-touching code satisfies the ticket procedurally. The automated gate itself is real follow-up work, not yet a story.

stories.title: One strict type-checking bar, with untyped externals walled off
stories.story: As a maintainer, I want the whole codebase held to one strict type-checking standard, with every place it touches an API the compiler cannot verify walled off behind a single typed boundary, so that a wrong assumption about another plugin's shape is caught while compiling, not when a user hits a crash.
stories.rationale: The target repository's tsconfig.json enables several of the strict-family flags individually but never sets the single "strict" option, and is missing others from that family. The old code reached into a companion plugin's internal state with a plain property read: one P1 defect read a Svelte store as if it were a plain object, and a feature it powered silently returned nothing for every user from the day it shipped.

acceptance_criteria.given: the TypeScript compiler configuration
then: strict mode is enabled as the single "strict" setting covering every strict sub-check
it is not a hand-picked subset of individually-enabled strict flags

acceptance_criteria.given: any function parameter, return value, or exported symbol in the codebase
then: no explicit or implicit "any" type is used to reach into a companion plugin's runtime object

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin needs data or a method from a companion plugin (Periodic Notes, Templater, or any other)
then: it is read only through a hand-written type describing the exact shape the plugin depends on
that type is defined in one place
every read of the companion plugin's state is validated or narrowed against that type before use

acceptance_criteria.given: a companion plugin's object does not match the expected shape at runtime (a missing method, a state container that requires an accessor instead of a direct property read, or an absent property)
then: the read is detected as invalid and handled explicitly
the depending feature is either disabled visibly or reports an explicit error
it does not silently return an empty or wrong result while appearing to have succeeded

acceptance_criteria.given: the build runs the compiler in strict mode over every first-party source file
acceptance_criteria.when: a type error exists anywhere under the plugin's own source
then: the build fails
it does not merely emit a warning while completing successfully

stories.title: Adding a granularity or a calendar indicator is a small, localised change
stories.story: As the person adding a new period type or a new calendar indicator later, I want that addition to touch a small, predictable set of files, so that extending Calendaric never means relearning or rewriting the whole plugin.
stories.rationale: In the target repository today, only day and week are functionally implemented anywhere; month, quarter, and year exist only as inert data shapes and permanently-disabled settings toggles. Separately, the old calendar-ui's indicator (calendar-source) contract was rewritten wholesale between two versions of the same library, forcing every one of its four real consumers to be rewritten rather than extended — the new contract must not repeat that failure mode.

acceptance_criteria.given: the set of supported period granularities
then: it requires one new entry in a single registry plus its own granularity-specific module
it requires no edit to the logic of any existing granularity's module

acceptance_criteria.given: the set of calendar indicators shown per day
then: it is implemented by one new module satisfying a documented indicator interface
it requires no change to the rendering code that already displays other indicators

acceptance_criteria.given: an indicator module written against the documented interface
acceptance_criteria.when: the interface changes in a later version
then: existing indicator modules either keep compiling unchanged, or fail to compile with a specific error naming the exact incompatibility
no existing indicator module changes behaviour silently at runtime as a result

acceptance_criteria.given: a new granularity or indicator is added and reviewed
acceptance_criteria.when: the change's file footprint is checked
then: it touches only its own new module, the single registry entry, and (for a granularity) that granularity's settings default
it does not touch the note-creation, parsing, or rendering logic belonging to an existing granularity or indicator

decisions.title: The indicator interface changes additively only
decisions.decision: Once published, the contract a calendar indicator implements only gains optional members. Removing or repurposing an existing member is a breaking change that requires a new contract alongside the old one.
decisions.rationale: The previous indicator contract was rewritten in a single version bump and broke every implementation at once. An additive-only rule is the cheapest guarantee that keeps that from repeating.

stories.title: A reproducible release build with every gate actually enforced
stories.story: As a release owner, I want one clean build to run every gate and produce every release artifact, so that releases are reproducible.
stories.rationale: AGENTS.md sets the manifest and versioning rules a release must satisfy. Elsewhere in the source material, the Periodic Notes fork had to drop lint from its build entirely because of a tooling bug, showing that a green build result does not by itself prove every gate ran. Separately, obsidian-daily-notes-interface needed a build-on-install script specifically so a consumer installing it directly from source would never silently receive unbuilt TypeScript in place of the compiled output.

acceptance_criteria.given: a clean checkout with only the pinned Node.js version installed
acceptance_criteria.when: the documented install-then-build commands are run
then: main.js, manifest.json, and styles.css (if present) are produced at the plugin root
no manual step beyond those commands is required

acceptance_criteria.given: manifest.json's id and version, and versions.json, ahead of a release
then: manifest.json's id is unchanged from the previous release
manifest.json's version follows semantic versioning
versions.json records this exact version mapped to the same minAppVersion declared in manifest.json

acceptance_criteria.given: a release has been tagged
acceptance_criteria.when: the release tag is compared against manifest.json
then: the tag matches manifest.json's version exactly, with no leading "v"

acceptance_criteria.given: manifest.json's minAppVersion for a release
acceptance_criteria.when: it is checked against the Obsidian APIs that release's code actually calls
then: a cited minimum-version source (Obsidian's own changelog or its API type definitions) justifies that minAppVersion
no API used by the release requires a newer Obsidian version than minAppVersion declares

acceptance_criteria.given: the build runs type-checking, linting, and the test suite
acceptance_criteria.when: any one of those three fails
then: the build as a whole is reported as failed
none of the three is skipped, disabled, or allowed to fail while the overall build still reports success

acceptance_criteria.given: one of the three gates cannot run because of a tooling defect
then: the build fails loudly
the failure message names which gate could not run

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin or any of its internal packages is installed directly from source rather than from a published release
then: the built output it depends on is produced automatically as part of the install
a consumer never receives unbuilt source in place of the compiled artefact

stories.title: Handle changes to Obsidian UI and other plugin APIs
stories.story: As a Calendaric user, I want the plugin to keep working, or fail visibly, when Obsidian changes its own UI internals or a companion plugin changes its internal state shape, so that an Obsidian or Periodic Notes update never leaves my settings screen crashed or a feature silently doing nothing.
stories.rationale: Two P1 defects show why this matters. An Obsidian 1.13 change to the settings dialog crashed the Periodic Notes settings pane. Another integration read a state container as a plain object instead of using its accessor or subscription API, so a shipped feature always returned nothing.

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin renders inside, or reads layout information from, an Obsidian-owned DOM element it does not control
acceptance_criteria.when: that element is absent or shaped differently than expected
then: the plugin skips the affected behaviour instead of throwing an unhandled error
no other part of the settings or view UI is left half-rendered as a result

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin reads state exposed by a companion plugin (a settings object, a store, a cache)
acceptance_criteria.when: that state is a container that must be read through its accessor or subscription API, not as a plain object
then: the plugin reads it through that store's own subscription or accessor mechanism
the plugin never treats it as a plain object with a direct property read

acceptance_criteria.given: a companion plugin's internal state does not expose the value the plugin expects, because it was renamed, restructured, or the companion plugin is absent
acceptance_criteria.when: the plugin tries to read it
then: the read returns a typed "unavailable" result
the depending feature is disabled visibly, or falls back to a documented default
it does not silently no-op while presenting as enabled

acceptance_criteria.given: a new version of Obsidian or a companion plugin changes a DOM structure or a data shape the plugin depends on
then: only the single adapter module written for that companion surface needs to change
no other module in the codebase reads that surface directly

stories.title: User-facing documentation matches verified behaviour
stories.story: As a Calendaric user reading the format-and-template guide, I want every behaviour it documents to match what the plugin actually does, so that I can trust the documentation instead of discovering the real behaviour by trial and error.
stories.rationale: The map found docs/guide.md stating that week tokens follow the user's configured week-start setting, while the code that resolves those tokens hard-codes ISO week numbering regardless of that setting — the documented and the implemented behaviour disagree today.

acceptance_criteria.given: a behaviour described in the user-facing guide
then: a test asserts the documented behaviour directly
the guide and the code cannot silently diverge without a test failing

acceptance_criteria.given: the "Start week on" setting is configured to a given day
acceptance_criteria.when: a week-based template token or a week number is resolved
then: it uses the day configured in "Start week on", never a fixed numbering independent of that setting
the guide states that week-based tokens and week numbers follow the configured "Start week on" day

acceptance_criteria.given: the guide is opened from within the plugin's settings
then: it works on every platform the manifest declares support for
opening the guide does not depend on a desktop-only capability when the manifest declares mobile support

acceptance_criteria.given: a documented setting, command, or behaviour is renamed, removed, or changed
then: the guide is updated in the same change
it is not left for a later, separate pass

acceptance_criteria.given: the guide describes a setting, command, or behaviour that no longer exists in the current settings schema or command list
acceptance_criteria.when: the guide is checked against the current implementation
then: the mismatch is detected before the release ships
the guide is corrected, or the removed item is restored, before the release ships

decisions.title: Week-based tokens and week numbers follow the configured week-start day
decisions.decision: The user's 'Start week on' setting is authoritative for week numbering and for the {{monday:fmt}}..{{sunday:fmt}} tokens, in both the filename format field and the note body. ISO week numbering is not hard-coded. The two surfaces must resolve the same weekday to the same date for the same setting.
decisions.rationale: The existing documentation already promises this and the code contradicts it. Keeping the promise is the smaller change and the honest one. In this vault the setting is Monday-first, so ISO and configured agree today and no existing note is affected. This settles which rule is correct; the Sunday-start case is verified by AC-TPL-03.2 against a live Sunday-first vault, and that criterion stays unverified until someone runs it.

stories.title: A budget-aware GitHub Actions workflow enforces the release build's gates on every pull request
stories.story: As a release owner on a free-tier GitHub account, I want every pull request to run the same install, lint, test and build gates automatically, so that a broken gate is caught before merge without relying on a human to run it locally, and without the workflow burning through a limited run-minute budget.
stories.rationale: No CI has ever run on this repository; ci.gates in the project's local tool config is provisional because it came from a local YAML parse rather than a real pipeline, and the account's Actions run-minutes are limited.

acceptance_criteria.given: a pull request is opened or updated against the default branch
then: it runs install, lint, test and build as one combined job
it reports one status check on the pull request for that job

acceptance_criteria.given: the workflow's trigger configuration
then: it triggers only on pull_request events
it does not trigger on every push to a branch that has no open pull request

acceptance_criteria.given: any one of install, lint, test or build fails during the workflow run
then: the status check reported on the pull request is failing
the workflow's own log names which step failed

acceptance_criteria.given: the workflow has completed at least one real run on a pull request
acceptance_criteria.when: the project's CI-gate detection is re-run afterward
then: it finds real pipeline or check-run data instead of falling back to a local YAML parse
the project's tool config can then be corrected from provisional to confirmed

notes: The two capability uids assigned to ARCH (forks:settings-tab-crash-guard-1.13, forks:git-dependency-self-build) are both single-defect fixes; every other criterion in this epic is derived directly from observations in calendaric-map.json rather than from a capability, per the schema's allowance for observation-derived criteria with covers left empty.

US-ARCH-05 (extensibility) and parts of US-ARCH-06 (release quality) are marked testable_by "manual" because verifying them means actually attempting the exercise (add a granularity, add an indicator, break a tooling gate) and reviewing the result's shape, not running an existing automated check.

tsconfig.json today enables several individual strict-family flags (noImplicitAny, noImplicitThis, strictNullChecks, strictBindCallApply, useUnknownInCatchVariables) but never sets the single "strict": true option, so it is missing others from that family (e.g. strictFunctionTypes, strictPropertyInitialization) implicitly. AC-ARCH-04.1 is written against the single-setting requirement rather than naming which flags are currently absent, since that list would go stale as the config changes.
No vault:* evidence-role capabilities were assigned to ARCH in epic-assignment.json, so no story carries a constrained_by entry.
